When you raise as many children, who are themselves able to reproduce, you "fulfill your purpose", so that your genefrom the perspective of natural selection is no more necessary for perpetuating itself than a worn-out shoe would be in continuing its existence. From an evolutionary standpoint indeed it makes sense. The idea here revolves around Darwin's theory which states: those organisms with traits best suited to their environment tend, on average over many generations and assuming random mating without sexual selection or natural disaster wiping out large portions of the population (such as a pandemic), leave more offspring than other individuals in that generation. In terms you're using - if we imagine our lives being like investments: each day is an investment. And just because your children are able to reproduce, doesn't mean they will pass on all or even most genes from their parents due the principle of genetic recombination during reproduction and natural selection favoring individuals with advantageous traits over others. Moreover it's important not only for survival but also health that organisms have a certain lifespan. If we were immortal (assuming no other changes to our biology), there would be many more diseases, including cancer which is caused by uncontrolled cell division - something the body has evolved mechanisms against in part because of its finite life span. In summary: from an evolutionary perspective it's beneficial for organisms not only as a species but also on individual level (health and survival) to have some form or length limit.
